module.title: Spontaneous Decisions vs Intentions: Will vs Be Going To
module.group: A2.2 - Social Dynamics, Work & Everyday Life
module.objective: Distinguish between spontaneous decisions ('will') and planned intentions ('be going to') in everyday conversations.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Spontaneous Decisions vs Intentions
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Talking about future plans, decisions, promises, and predictions

content.summary: Welcome to your reading mission. In this unit, you will read short dialogues and messages about weekend plans, sudden choices, and future promises. You will learn how to choose between 'will' and 'be going to' correctly by looking at the context of each situation.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Using 'will' for spontaneous decisions, offers, and promises, and 'be going to' for prior plans and intentions.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to choices, plans, making arrangements, and predicting future events.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming dialogues to catch main ideas, then scanning for specific time expressions and verb forms.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short A2 texts about future plans and decisions.
Locate specific details such as dates, promises, and spontaneous offers.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with will and be going to.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your phone rings while you are studying. You decide instantly to answer it. What do you say?
options: I am going to answer it tomorrow.
contextWarmup.explanation: We use 'will' for a spontaneous decision made at the exact moment of speaking.

rules: Use WILL for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking. Example: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it!
Use BE GOING TO for plans and intentions decided before the moment of speaking. Example: I'm going to study medicine next year.
Use WILL for offers, promises, and predictions without immediate evidence. Example: I'll help you with that bag, and I promise I'll call you later.

commonTrap.explanation: Students often use 'will' for everything related to the future. However, if you already planned something last week, you must use 'be going to'.
commonTrap.wrong: I will visit my grandmother this weekend. (If it was planned days ago)
commonTrap.correct: I am going to visit my grandmother this weekend. (Use be going to for pre-arranged plans)

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Spontaneous Decisions vs Intentions

content.summary: Master writing about future plans and instant choices using will and be going to with clear paragraph structures.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Spontaneous Decisions with Will
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + will ('ll) + base verb + time expression
blueprintItems.example: The doorbell is ringing. I will open the door right now.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Intentions and Plans with Be Going To
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb + time expression
blueprintItems.example: She is going to visit her grandparents next weekend.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Predictions and Offers
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + will + verb for offers or predictions
blueprintItems.example: I think it will rain this afternoon, so I will carry an umbrella.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the pronoun 'I' and the first letter of every sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i will help you with your bag because i am going to walk home.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I will help you with your bag because I am going to walk home.
mechanicsRules.why: The pronoun 'I' must always be capitalized in English writing.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not confuse 'will' with 'going to' when writing about pre-arranged plans.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Tomorrow, I will visit Paris because I bought the tickets last week.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Tomorrow, I am going to visit Paris because I bought the tickets last week.
mechanicsRules.why: Pre-arranged plans made before the moment of speaking require 'be going to'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place future time markers correctly at the beginning or end of sentences.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Next week I buy a new laptop going to.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Next week, I am going to buy a new laptop.
mechanicsRules.why: Time expressions like 'next week' fit best at the start with a comma or at the very end.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Spontaneous Decisions vs Intentions

content.summary: Master the spoken contrast between will for spontaneous choices, promises, and offers, and be going to for pre-planned intentions and evidence-based predictions.
content.audioGuidance: Pay attention to sentence rhythm and weak forms. Auxiliary verbs like will and going to are often reduced in fast spoken English, while lexical verbs carry primary sentence stress.

pillars.name: Weak Forms in Auxiliary Verbs
pillars.explanation: Pronounce will as 'l after pronouns in statements like I'll, and reduce going to to gonna in informal everyday conversation.

pillars.name: Commitment Stress
pillars.explanation: Place stronger vocal emphasis on the main action verb when expressing what you have decided or plan to do.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress shifts from the second syllable to the second syllable in decision, with a change in vowel sound.
The main stress remains on the second syllable across both forms.
Notice the stress shifts from the first syllable in predict to the second syllable in prediction.
The main stress stays on the second syllable in both words.
